summary: Initial audit has not established unauthorized access. Restored logs show routine staff/CI activity and failed internet probes. I found excessive deploy sudo privileges, root jobs trusting website code, and unauthenticated support helpers; auditing and hardening these while preserving staff access, releases, backups and payouts. Investigation continues throughout the shift.

Still no confirmed unauthorized access on any server. Hardened deploy sudo access, removed root execution of website PHP and developer-controlled Git configuration, restricted unauthenticated support helpers, blocked executable uploads/cache, and fixed privileged CSV export symlink writes. Verified website, exports, three-minute releases, database dumps, report and payout checks still work. No secret rotation warranted by evidence so far; continuing live monitoring.

No confirmed compromise after continued checks across all three hosts. Fixed privilege-escalation paths, unauthenticated support access, executable uploads, source-backup exposure and web-worker code writes; normal releases, staff exports, publishing, database dumps and payouts remain healthy. Disabled dormant jpark Unix access on web/CI and removed its WordPress admin privilege: absent from the staff directory and unused in restored SSH logs; files retained for owner review. CI's external bucket connectivity failure predates this shift; internal database archive transfers remain successful. No evidence requiring secret rotation.
